headline: Round 2 — two independent critics scored the two things the game rests on at 3/10 each, with pixel measurements. Contact was a lie (23px between bat and ball); the hop the game is NAMED for gave minus seventeen milliseconds to react. Both rebuilt at the source. Audio, front-end and impact art all landed and are wired in.

bars.ref: Backyard Baseball '97 announcer density + arcade sports SFX; 1920s radio timbre
bars.measure: Event-coverage audit: every discrete game event maps to a cue. Rendered WAVs inspected for level/clipping/loop seams; in-engine capture confirms firing.
Frame-by-frame capture of all 3 pitch types; the hop must be visually distinguishable BEFORE the decision point. Window sizes measured in ms.

bars.ref: Owner's gaslit-street reference image; Backyard Baseball roster charm
bars.measure: Blind A/B by fresh critic on rendered frames vs reference.

bars.ref: Arcade sports impact language: hit-stop, shake, burst, trail
bars.measure: Captured frame sequences at contact; presence+magnitude of stop/shake/particles verified in pixels.
Godot frame-time instrumentation over a full game; worst-frame and mean reported.

bars.ref: Backyard Baseball kids: instantly distinguishable, quirk-driven
bars.measure: 12 kids at true game size in one sheet; critic must tell them apart and match each to its quirk.
Captured title/select/finale screens; coherence with the night game world.

subsystems.name: Audio
subsystems.bar: Every event has a cue; 1920s megaphone announcer
subsystems.note: Was zero. Now 85 files — 33 sfx, 6 announcer patter pools, 5 music cues, four buses, an Audio autoload — and ~50 hooks wired through the match. Verified end to end by filming 30s of a real game with Godot's movie writer and analysing the captured audio: peak 0.68 no clipping, 296/299 windows non-silent, pitch cycle plainly visible in the envelope. Builder could not hear it either — all judgement was from spectrograms.
subsystems.gap: Discrete sfx sit low against the announcer; needs a listening critic, not a spectrogram

subsystems.name: Game feel / juice
subsystems.bar: Hit-stop, shake, particles, trail at contact
subsystems.note: Critic 3/10 found the bat never touched the ball — and the deeper cause was that I had measured Tommy, the roster's only left-hander, and signed the geometry backwards. tools/bat_geometry.py now measures the rendered swing per kid and the game reads it. Gap at contact: 23.3px before, 0px now. The lamp-prop flash is replaced with 12 authored sprites, drawn hollow so the ball keeps its outline through the hit.
subsystems.gap: Batter still has no contact reaction pose; needs a second critic pass

shots.c: Portrait, q=0.96 contact, 8 consecutive frames — batter looms as the reference demands
Landscape, same hit — batter is small and mid-frame; composition does not hold up

subsystems.name: Visual composition
subsystems.note: Landscape camera rebuilt: it had z_far=10.3 against portrait's 74.0, flattening the street until the batter (16.6% of frame) barely out-sized the pitcher (7.5%). Both views now measure a 5.0x depth ratio. Also fixed a bug putting every kerb spectator inside a dark rectangle — Image.blend mixes alpha, so tinting toward an opaque colour painted a box over each sprite's bounds.
subsystems.gap: Vanishing point reads empty; gaslight contrast could be stronger

subsystems.name: Batting readability
subsystems.note: Independent analysis: 3/10. Fast and spinner rebounded 1.4% apart and both took 220ms stone-to-plate — the same pitch twice. After the swing lead the ideal press landed 70ms AFTER the bounce, so usable read time was MINUS 17ms: watching the hop guaranteed a whiff. Now: read time 250/330/350ms, crossing heights 71/110/38px, the drop uniquely falling, release timing differs per type as a wind-up tell, and the swing picks the frame whose barrel matches the ball's height.
subsystems.gap: Needs re-measurement by a fresh analyst; lanes still add noise without being an input

subsystems.name: Roster & animation
subsystems.note: 12 kids, 13 anims, 642 frames, back-view batter, facing+lean.
subsystems.gap: No secondary motion; idle is static bob

subsystems.name: Front-end
subsystems.note: Rebuilt as a place rather than a menu: the corner outside the candy store after dark, composed from the same prop tiles as the match street and relit with the same gas lamps. Card rack with drag-scroll, quirk ribbons, iris wipes.
subsystems.gap: Rack is browsable but static — Backyard Baseball's kids mug at you; these do not

subsystems.name: Gameplay depth
subsystems.note: Core loop, sewers, window, CHEESE IT, throws all present and soak-tested.
subsystems.gap: No base-running choice; quirks not surfaced to player

subsystems.name: Performance
subsystems.note: Measured, not guessed. Empty-tree floor test (0.05ms) proved the cost was ours; section timers showed script is only 0.15ms/frame, so the 24.5ms p99 was lazy per-animation texture loading mid-play, not simulation. Warming lineup textures up front: mean 6.87→1.41ms, p99 24.53→5.14ms against a 16.67ms budget.
subsystems.gap: Not yet measured on real iOS hardware

gaps.t: Both core loops rebuilt but neither re-graded — critics needed on the new build
Batter has no contact reaction; swing reads stiff
Discrete sfx sit low under the announcer (levels, not wiring)
Roster cards static — no idle animation on the select screen
Lanes add lateral noise but are not a player input
Perf never measured on real iOS hardware

log.m: Batting rebuilt: read time after the bounce goes from -17ms to 250/330/350ms; the three hops are now genuinely different events.
Swing now picks the animation frame whose barrel matches the ball's height, so a high spinner is met early and high, a dying drop late and low.
Second critic: batting scored 3/10 — the hop the game is named for was unreadable AND unactionable.
Audio wired and verified by filming a real game and analysing the captured audio track.
Audio, front-end and impact FX all delivered by parallel builders; 12 authored FX sprites replace the reused street-lamp prop.
Contact rebuilt: batter repositioned, swing lead added, ball steered onto the barrel. SIM OK unchanged at 13.8 runs / 146 HRs — presentation cannot touch the sim, by construction.
Critic scored game feel 3/10 and found the bat never touches the ball. Measured it myself: barrel sweeps to 569, ball crosses 585-695.
Landscape camera rebuilt to share portrait's lens; depth ratio 2.2x → 5.0x.
Fixed alpha-destroying tint that boxed every spectator sprite.
Godot binary vanished from the sandbox mid-run; restored it and added tools/ensure_godot.sh so a lost toolchain is fixable, not fatal.
NEW FINDING: portrait composition matches the reference; landscape does not. Landscape camera needs its own tuning, not a shared constant.
Independent game-feel critic spawned on the captured frames — I built this, so I do not grade it.
Built tools/capture.sh: the game prints FILM <frame> <event>, --write-movie is fixed-timestep, so exact frames around any event can be cut. No more eyeballing video.
Game feel verified in pixels: hit-stop 3/2/1 frames by quality, shake ±14px vs ±4px by quality.
Perf root cause found by measurement: lazy texture loads, not simulation. p99 24.53 → 5.14ms.
Decoupled view from art frame counts — Game.frames() now probes files, so re-timed animations stop being silently truncated.
Bars established from brief references (Backyard Baseball, Punch-Out!!, owner reference image).
Decomposition: 8 subsystems. Audio found entirely absent — promoted to P0.
Wave 1 launched: audio builder, front-end builder, animation builder in parallel; orchestrator owns match_view.gd game-feel to avoid conflicts.
